## Professional Experience

**CNRS** — *Post-doc* — 2026–present

Reporting to: Daniele Raimondi.  
Location: CNRS UMR-IGMM, Montpellier, France.

- Research project on the inclusion of mixed effects in neural networks.
- Implemented a mixed model solver performing REML on GPU.
    - More than 12 times faster (running on A100 GPU) than the state-of-the-art software Wombat (running on 64 CPUs) on a GBLUP benchmark.
    - Implements a wide range of mixed model specification, as listed in [pyreml]{.pyreml}'s [doc](https://ai-for-genome-interpretation-lab.github.io/pyreml/variance_structures.html)

**Seenovate** — *Data Science Consultant* — 2023–2026  

Reporting to: Frank Imbach.  
Location: Montpellier, France.

- Developed AI/ML products for clients and for internal projects.
- Led the development of a platform delivering statistical inference from agronomical trials to an Agritech client, now used daily.
Supervised other 4 developpers for 260 days over 3 years.
- Led research projects and kept a publication record.
- Delivered training on statistical modeling to academic research centers.

**Limagrain** — *Researcher in Statistics* — 2018–2022

Reporting to: Nicolas Heslot.  
Location: Chappes Research Center, Clermont-Ferrand, France.

- Led genomic breeding projects, including a pilot, highly challenging maize breeding program:
    - Data-driven genomic breeding decisions,
    - Monitoring of field and greenhouse operations,
    - Management of a maize breeding technician,
    - Management of a 230 k€/year budget.
- Contributed to a global platform serving genomic inference to international business teams (300+ users). My role included scientific overseeing and development.
- Led ***Confidential*** research & reported internally. Contributed to change adoption across the organization.

**Biogemma** — *Researcher in Bioinformatics* — 2018, 7 months  

Reporting to: Pierre Dubreuil.  
Location: Chappes Research Center, Clermont-Ferrand, France.

- Research project on leveraging the haplotype block genome structure in GWAS.

**INRAE** — *PhD Student* — 2014–2017

Reporting to: Leopoldo Sánchez and Luc Pâques.  
Location: INRAE UR-AGPF, Orléans, France.

- Parameterized a Bayesian multivariate model for the prediction of reaction norms. Inferred genetic parameters and heterosis as longitudinal trajectories.
- Adapted a water availability model to forest tree plantations at the individual tree level.
- Demonstrated that the *Larix* genetic contrasts (heterosis and individual breeding values) were amplified with higher water availability (*i.e.* better growth conditions).
- Contributed to the field data collection (about 3 weeks in the forest plantations) and curation.

**Cirad** — *MSc Internship* — 2014, 6 months

Reporting to: David Cros  
Location: Cirad UMR-AGAP, Montpellier, France.

- Investigation on the performance of bivariate mixed models in application to oil palm breeding.

## Teaching

**Seenovate** — 2023–2026  

Training supervision: Jérôme-Philippe Garsi.  
Location: At the client, all of France.

*Statistics* and statistical software (R) — animated 17 training sessions for a total of 44 days, with an average satisfaction grade of 8.9/10. Some trainings were not graded.
With a conversion from days to hour of 7h/day (which is an approximation, some days were longer and some were shorter), the corresponding volume is **308 hours**.
